#3391. Report: Apple faces congressional scrutiny over ICE tracking apps and Trump donations

Reuters and The Washington Post report that Apple is among the tech giants potentially facing congressional investigations as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers in January. Here are the details.

Earlier today, The Washington Post reported that “Democrats are laying the groundwork to investigate some of the country’s largest companies, setting off a scramble among executives who courted the president.”

The report notes that Washington law firms are advising companies and executives on how to prepare for potential congressional investigations, with some also pitching their services to Elon Musk:

Multiple firms have crafted pitches for why they should serve as Musk’s personal counsel, aware that the world’s richest man is likely to receive a barrage of subpoenas and that any casework stemming from those investigations will be both lucrative and the highest-profile investigative work available in the coming year, according to two of the people.

When it comes to Apple, the report noted that lawmakers are gearing up to investigate the company “over its hosting of tracking apps used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.”

While the report refers to Apple’s hosting of tracking apps used by ICE, the company has previously faced scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over its decision to remove apps used to track ICE agents from the App Store.

Last year, Apple removed ICEBlock and several similar apps from the App Store following pressure from the DOJ, citing concerns over the safety of federal agents.

The move came shortly after a gunman opened fire on an ICE facility in Dallas, ultimately killing two detainees in an attack that federal authorities described as targeted violence against ICE.

Since then, Apple has faced questions from Democratic lawmakers over the extent of the Trump administration’s involvement in the decision and whether the removals infringed on constitutionally protected speech.

 or no , oversight needs to happen. If  did bad, let it come out; if not, let that come out as well. There should be no sacred cows here, oversight and accountability need to be our national, collective goal. Anyone who says otherwise is trying to sell you something.

Reuters, meanwhile, reported that Senator Richard Blumenthal, “who is set to take over as chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations,” called on Apple “and others who donated to [President Trump’s new White House] ballroom project to turn over records” or “face possible subpoenas in January.”

As The Washington Post reported last month, Apple and Nvidia each pledged $25 million toward the ballroom, making them two of the project’s largest donors.

Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters or The Washington Post.

#3389. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

This week, Apple released the first iOS 27.3 beta. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left to make it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

#3388. Aura Ink 10 review: A digital photo frame that looks (almost) like a real picture

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Aura Ink 10 is a second-generation ePaper photo frame that’s smaller and less expensive than the original, and can display a few more colors. If you’re looking for a digital photo frame you can hang on your wall without any wires showing, this is the one to get, though it is more expensive than most other frames, and overall it's less vibrant than a traditional digital photo frame.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

A year ago, Aura introduced the Aura Ink, the first ePaper photo frame; this device, while not as vibrant as a traditional digital photo frame, had the advantage of letting you hang it on a wall — no power cord required — for up to three months at a time without needing to be recharged.

The company is back with the Aura Ink 10, the first in the second generation of ePaper style photo frames. This frame can show more colors, and at $349, is also less expensive, albeit still well above some of the best digital photo frames. So, is the premium worth it?

The Aura Ink 10 went on sale on November 10, 2026, for $349 at Aura's website. It’s offered in just one size, and with just one matte color (black). The original only came with a white matte; I wish the company offered both options.

The frame itself is very thin, at a little less than an inch, and comes with both a stand for placing it on a table, as well as pins so you can mount it on a wall. Three buttons sit inconspicuously on the back edge of the frame, and let you switch photos and get the frame ready to go. Overall, it’s a very subtle design, and it’s unlikely that anyone would recognize it as a digital frame at a glance.

The Aura Ink 10 uses an E Ink Spectra 6 display, which can produce nine colors (black, white, red, yellow, blue, green, off-white, mustard yellow and orange), up from six on the original Aura Ink. That means it can show more nuances in pictures, though don’t expect true-to-life fidelity that you would get from a traditional LCD picture frame. The 10-inch frame also has the same resolution as the 13-inch model, which means greater pixel density.

To see the difference in Aura Ink generations, I placed the 10-inch Ink next to the 13-inch Ink, and then displayed the same photos on each.

The 10 inch model tended to show photos a little darker, but with better transitions between light and dark areas. For example, in an image of a girl jumping off a sand dune, there was less obvious pixelation from the sun-drenched stretches of the beach to shaded areas.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

In another photo of a girl in front of a blue and white wall, the blues of the wall were a bit deeper, but shadows were more pronounced, making it more difficult to make out features in her face and neck area.

The Aura Ink 10 has very gentle lighting that only turns on if it senses someone in front of the frame. Again, it’s not something you’d notice unless you see it turn on, but it helps bring a little more vibrancy to the photo.

Aura says the Ink 10 will last up to three months on a charge, assuming it changes photos just once per day. Once it runs low, you simply have to plug it into a USB-C for a little bit.

Aura also updated the manner in which the frame refreshes; on the original model, the screen kind of flashes randomly as the photo changes. On the Ink 10, there’s a wave-like pattern that starts in one corner, and ripples across the screen. It’s more intentional, and doesn’t make it look like the frame is shorting out.

One thing that Aura does well is make it easy to add photos to its devices. For starters, you can sync your iCloud or Google Photos albums in the Aura app. And, to help narrow things down, the Aura app can filter photos by person, so that you can more easily find photos of particular individuals; unfortunately, there’s no pet filter. If you want to skip the app entirely, you can also either email or text photos to the display. Handy!

As someone who tests smart home devices for a living, I suspect my house, which has smart displays everywhere, is a bit different than most. So while I appreciate traditional digital photo frames — the Alexa Photo Frame is one of my favorites, for its innovative use of AI — it’s nice to have some tech that doesn’t look like tech.

Yes, there are some tradeoffs to an ePaper photo display like the Aura Ink 10. You’re not going to get colors that really fly off the screen, and you’re going to pay a premium over other photo frames. But, in a digital-everything world, I appreciate its subtleness.

#3385. This TP-Link Wi-Fi 7 Travel Router Is 27% Off for This Early Black Friday Deal

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $87.99 from $119.99 in an early Black Friday deal—marking its lowest price to date, according to price trackers. This is not a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas so it slips easily into a bag.

More about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

#3382. Apple TV renews ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ for season three

Award-winning culinary show ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ is getting a third season, in an announcement that came hours after its second season came to a close. Here are the details.

Just as ‘Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook’ premiered with a two-episode combo, and ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ aired its second season finale, the company confirmed that the latter will return for an eight-episode third season.

‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ is hosted by Topjaw’s Jesse Burgess and executive produced by Gordon Ramsay. Each season tells the story of several restaurants around the world as they compete to earn, retain, or increase their Michelin Star ratings.

The show premiered on Apple TV in 2025 to a perfect 100% Tomatometer score and has since been nominated for a BAFTA Television Award in the Factual Entertainment category, and won Best Popular Factual Programme at the 2026 Broadcast Digital Awards.

With eight episodes in each season, the show has taken viewers inside some of the world’s most acclaimed restaurants, including Brazil’s Evvai, the first in Latin America to earn three Michelin Stars, and Ynyshir, a two-star restaurant in rural Wales.

“What I love most about making ‘Knife Edge’ is that, however much time I spend in restaurants around the world, I’m constantly surprised by the extraordinary people and stories we discover. Behind every restaurant is a very personal journey, and for the chefs we follow, a Michelin Star can represent years of sacrifice, obsession and an enormous amount of hard work. It’s a privilege to be able to tell these stories, and I’m absolutely thrilled that we get to do it all again for a third season”

#3381. There's a New Way to Automatically Back Up Your Android Photos for Free

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you're an Android user looking for a way to save your photos and videos without maxing out your cloud storage space, your device may soon be able to back up automatically to your PC. As spotted by Android Authority, Google included automatic backups from Android to Windows via Quick Share in its release notes for Google Play services v26.43.

Quick Share is a wireless file-sharing feature for Android that allows users to send photos, videos, and documents to nearby devices, including Windows computers and iPhones with AirDrop. The new automatic backup feature, which is likely to roll out gradually, uses Quick Share's functionality to transfer copies of photos and videos on your phone to your PC when nearby.

Since these backups happen locally, you don't need to rely solely on cloud storage in your Google account, nor do you need to remember to initiate transfers of photos and videos between devices. Plus, this is all free and doesn't require a separate cloud service subscription. While you can back up your media to Google Photos, as of earlier this year, more data from your Android backups count toward your Google Account storage cap unless you exclude specific types. Alternatively, you can also cobble together a decent amount of cloud storage from other providers at no extra cost, but automatic backups between Android and Windows minimize the likelihood that you'll forget to save data, and your PC provides plenty of space for free.

Once the feature is available on your device, you'll be able to initiate backups in the Quick Share for Windows app. Your Android and Windows devices must be in close proximity and signed into the same Google Account. You can toggle Automatic backups on and change the settings for what gets backed up and to where. The transfers will then occur wirelessly in the background.

As Android Authority reports, early hints at this feature suggested that Samsung phones and PCs would be excluded from automatic backups, but the release notes don't specify any further details.

#3380. Kylie Jenner Sued by Housekeeper Who Says Mogul’s Dog Bit Her

Kylie Jenner is facing a new lawsuit from a former housekeeper who claims she was mistreated while working for the cosmetics mogul and received only lip service and an eventual pink slip when she complained.

The new legal action from plaintiff Dinora Cabria Amaya follows two other similar lawsuits that were filed against Jenner last April. While the new 20-page complaint obtained by Rolling Stone doesn’t accuse Jenner of first-hand mistreatment, it suggests the reality star played a role in decisions regarding scheduling, supervision, and allegedly unlawful wage practices.

Cabria Amaya, who started working for Jenner in March 2025, claims she was denied overtime and subjected to a hostile work environment. She also claims she suffered multiple workplace injuries that were mishandled. On Sept. 4, 2025, for example, Cabria Amaya says she was cleaning a laundry room when an unsecured can of pepper spray allegedly discharged directly into her face and eyes, causing “severe burning and vision problems” that she reported to her supervisor via text.

“Sorry to interrupt you, I had an accident at work, someone left pepper spray and took off safety,” she wrote in the message, according to the lawsuit. Her manager allegedly responded, “thanks for letting us know.” Cabria Amaya says she was asked to fill out a report and give it to Jenner’s security before visiting a doctor. She later received no accommodations when she reported experiencing “significant eye pain, blurred vision, headaches, burning, irritation, and sensitivity” that affected her performance, her lawsuit filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court by attorney Della Shaker claims.

“The more plaintiff complained that she was hurt, the harder defendants made her job,” the lawsuit states. Cabria Amaya and her lawyer claim she was sometimes “confined in a room because defendant Jenner did not want to see her,” and that her “repeated reports of ongoing pain” were never taken seriously or accommodated. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

On one occasion, the lawsuit states, she used a passcode to enter Jenner’s closet but became locked inside where she began to suffer a panic attack. “No one is at the house that can let you out and I cannot give the password to anyone else, you just have to wait,” her manager allegedly replied when Cabria Amaya called to inform her. The manager purportedly “mocked her” during the call, she says.

Later, on Oct. 28, 2025, Cabria Amaya was cleaning a doghouse when Jenner’s dog allegedly bit her. She immediately reported the incident to her manager, the lawsuit states.

“Again, no meaningful assistance was provided. Plaintiff purchased over-the-counter medication and treated the injury herself,” the lawsuit claims. “She continued reporting that her eyes hurt, her arm and wrist hurt from the dog bite, and her back hurt from the increasingly physical work.”

Cabria Amaya was terminated on Feb. 6, 2026, after requesting that she be paid mileage for trips between Jenner’s houses to complete various tasks assigned during a single shift. She now believes she was fired because she spoke up about her wages and workplace treatment, the lawsuit says.

The lawsuit names Jenner, her company Kylie Jenner Inc., staff supervisors Laura Dooley and Itzel Sibrian, Tri Star Services, and La Maison Family Services as defendants. It includes claims for wrongful termination, false imprisonment, disability discrimination, failure to provide reasonable accommodations, whistleblower retaliation, failure to prevent discrimination and retaliation, and intentional infliction of emotional distress. It’s seeking unpaid wages, past and future lost earnings, and compensatory and punitive damages to be determined at trial. Jenner’s lawyer, Michael Rhodes, says in a statement to Rolling Stone that the new claims were filed by the same lawyer who is representing the other housekeepers who sued her earlier this year.

“It’s clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday,” he tells Rolling Stone in a statement. “We’re not going to be intimidated into doing that. As such, we’ll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story.”

Cabria Amaya’s lawyer, meanwhile, says she’s not backing down. “For employees working in high-profile households, the fear of losing future employment opportunities can be overwhelming. When your livelihood depends on discretion, references, and powerful professional relationships, speaking out can feel impossible. But no employer has the right to retaliate against workers for protected complaints,” she tells Rolling Stone in a statement. “The truth should never be buried behind wealth, fear, or silence.”

The new complaint from Cabria Amaya comes after former housekeepers Angelica Hernandez Vasquez and Juana Delgado Soto filed similar lawsuits against Jenner last April. All three women allege mistreatment and whistleblower retaliation.

Delgado Soto claimed that after her request to attend her brother’s funeral was denied, she left a desperate note for Jenner on a massage table shortly before the makeup magnate was due to receive a treatment. “I need to express just how terribly I am mentally abused,” the letter said, according to the lawsuit. “I really apologize for letting you know about all these situations, I know you wouldn’t allow this to happen, if you were aware of it.”

According to her lawsuit, Delgado Soto was threatened with termination the next day and instructed never to contact Jenner again. A hearing in that case is set for March 22, 2027.

#3378. Windows Laptops Just Closed a Major Gap With the MacBook Neo

To say the MacBook Neo disrupted the laptop market would be an understatement. When the Neo dropped, former Apple CEO Tim Cook said Apple had its best-ever launch week for first-time Mac customers, and the company is reportedly planning on doubling the MacBook's sales for 2027. It's not hard to see why the MacBook Neo is such a hit: Apple is offering the essential Mac experience at a fantastic price point. You no longer need to spend $1,000 or more for a MacBook, so long as you're okay making some sacrifices to get there—which, it seems, many customers are.

While the MacBook Neo has been a boon for Apple and Apple fans alike, I can only imagine the stress it brought to PC manufacturers—especially those with budget or midrange machines. Windows PCs have long won the price war against Apple. While MacBooks have their passionate customers, buyers looking for the best value have had to weigh expensive Apple laptops against many far cheaper options from companies like Dell, HP, ASUS, and Lenovo. But with the Neo, suddenly a MacBook was competing in this space, and well.

Part of the issue for PC manufacturers was Apple's control over its own ecosystem. Unlike most PC makers, which only produce the hardware for each machine, Apple makes both the hardware and the software for its MacBook lineup. As such, the company has the advantage of optimizing that hardware. It can design macOS to run more efficiently on weaker hardware, in a way that companies like Dell or ASUS can't. You might be comparing the MacBook Neo against a Windows laptop with similar specs, or even better specs, but because Microsoft makes Windows, not the laptop manufacturer, it's possible the Neo ends up with the better overall experience. While that might still be the case, Microsoft may have just closed that gap in a meaningful way.

This week, Microsoft announced key upgrades to memory-management efficiency, particularly for machines with 8GB of RAM. This is the amount of memory the MacBook Neo has, as well as many budget and midrange Windows laptops. That's not much memory for 2026, regardless of platform, but Apple seems to have squeezed a lot out of it for the Neo. Now, Microsoft may have just done the same for PCs, as Windows is reportedly 20% more responsive, with 40% faster multitasking.

In its blog post, Microsoft highlighted improvements that users with 8 GB of RAM can expect from Windows going forward. First, Microsoft says it focused on better utilizing the RAM your machine already has. The company compares its memory management to a desk: Anything on the "desk" is stored in RAM; anything in your "drawer" is stored in your drive. As you use your PC, Windows used to move more of your apps and tabs to your drawer to free up more RAM for other things, meaning you'd need to reload those items whenever you returned to them. Going forward, the company says that Windows can keep up to 2GB more of your active data in RAM instead of moving it to slower storage elsewhere. That means apps and tabs should refresh less frequently when you leave and return to them.

Microsoft also says that small actions should be faster across the board. When you open the Start menu, search across your PC, right-click, open Settings, launch the Snipping Tool, and open File Explorer, those actions may be up to 20% faster than they were in January. Microsoft Edge may open up to 33% faster, while Teams can enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, which means it can launch up to 20% faster too. Microsoft put together an interesting stress test to compare multitasking performance between today and January. It opened 20 tabs in Edge, a 4K video, large Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, then Outlook and File Explorer, all without closing any windows. That experience was 40% faster following this latest update.

Microsoft says it also improved the memory efficiency in its apps: The company claims it reduced committed-memory growth by up to 900 MB, and saved up to 360 MB in RAM across Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook. That extends to third-party apps as well: Microsoft says that WhatsApp has double-digit memory improvement now. Widgets also only load when you open the app, which saves 200 MB of RAM when the app is closed, while Edge tabs go inactive after 15 minutes instead of two hours.

Microsoft isn't making these upgrades in a vacuum. Hardware costs, particularly for RAM, have skyrocketed in the age of AI. Microsoft knows that people are likely going to hold onto existing hardware for longer than they usually do, or that they'll opt for less-expensive configurations, including, perhaps, machines with 8 GB of RAM.

PCMag's Chris Hoffman was adamant before this latest Windows update that buyers should steer clear of PCs with 8 GB of RAM. Now, he's pulling back a bit. In his testing, Hoffman noticed improvements when multitasking on an 8 GB PC when compared to similar tests from months ago. He could run multiple Chrome tabs, a Microsoft Word window, and Spotify without bogging down the computer much. Hoffman isn't a lightweight user, so he still wouldn't personally choose an 8 GB machine, but he admits, "If I were an average PC buyer looking for a reasonable desktop experience and could save hundreds of dollars by opting for 8GB of RAM, I might be happy with the performance."

To that point, I think this new Windows update makes 8 GB PCs competitive, especially against the MacBook Neo. We'll still need direct comparisons to know how well this new Windows experience holds up across the board, but these updates are promising. Users with 8 GB machines just got a free, valuable update overnight; new customers can opt for a more affordable PC without feeling like performance will take a nosedive just because they opened one too many Edge tabs.

As Hoffman says, 8 GB of RAM is not ideal for any user looking for serious multitasking or professional workflows, regardless of whether they choose a Mac or PC. But for the average computer customer looking for a solid machine without breaking the bank, I no longer see the Neo as necessarily the default choice. After all, Apple has slowly raised its price, too, from $599 to $699. If you're platform-agnostic, or even prefer Windows to macOS, these updates from Microsoft are quite promising. If you're in the market, check out PCMag's excellent list of budget laptop recommendations.
